deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.2 端緒 — Vocabulary
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第二章「端緒」
notes: Vocabulary for Chapter 2. 瀧 wakes up in 三葉's body in her mountain town, and 三葉 wakes up in his in Tokyo — crowded trains, stylish cafés, his waiter job, and the night she rescues 奥寺先輩's slashed skirt with a needle — until notes, phone diary entries and friends' reports convince them both that the 'dream' is real. The deck focuses on bewilderment and realisation, body and mirror, Tokyo life, restaurant work and sewing, and the gender-speech gap. It is built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style, not transcribed page by page, so a few words may turn up a chapter early or late. Example sentences are original, not quoted from the book. Words and patterns already taught in an earlier chapter's deck aren't repeated here, even when this chapter uses them again.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.scene: The chapter title — the first strange morning that sets the whole body-swap story in motion.
cards.context: 端 (edge, end) + 緒 (the end of a thread or cord, as in へその緒): the loose end you can pull to unravel something — fitting for a story about braided cords. Also read たんちょ. Typical use: 事件の端緒をつかむ 'get the first lead in a case'.
cards.example_sentence: 小さな違和感が、すべての謎を解く端緒になった。
cards.example_reading: ちいさな いわかん が、 すべて の なぞ を とく たんしょ に なった。
cards.example_meaning: A small feeling that something was off became the first clue to solving the whole mystery.

cards.scene: 瀧 wakes up — but in a room, and a body, that are not his.
cards.context: More literary than 目が覚める or 起きる, so narration likes it. Also figurative: 才能に目覚める 'discover a talent'. Noun 目覚め; 目覚まし時計 = alarm clock.
cards.example_sentence: 目覚めると、窓の外で鳥が鳴いていた。
cards.example_reading: めざめる と、 まど の そと で とり が ないて いた。
cards.example_meaning: When I woke, birds were singing outside the window.

cards.scene: 瀧 opens his eyes in an unfamiliar room in a mountain town he has never seen.
cards.context: An old negative form (ぬ = ない) that only goes before nouns: 見知らぬ人 'a stranger', 見知らぬ町. Written/literary — in speech you'd say 知らない. Compare 見慣れない 'not used to seeing'.
cards.example_sentence: 見知らぬ人に道を聞かれて、少し驚いた。
cards.example_reading: みしらぬ ひと に みち を きかれて、 すこし おどろいた。
cards.example_meaning: I was a little surprised when a stranger asked me for directions.

cards.scene: Still groggy, 瀧 assumes the strange room and body must be part of a dream.
cards.context: 寝ぼけて〜 = did something while half-awake. 寝ぼけてるの？ is the natural teasing 'Are you still asleep?' for someone acting oddly in the morning. 寝ぼけ眼 (ねぼけまなこ) = sleepy eyes.
cards.example_sentence: 寝ぼけて、弟の靴をはいて家を出てしまった。
cards.example_reading: ねぼけて、 おとうと の くつ を はいて いえ を でて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: Half-asleep, I left the house wearing my little brother's shoes.

cards.scene: Everything feels wrong to 瀧 — the weight of the body, the long hair, the voice.
cards.context: 違 (differ) + 和 (harmony) + 感 (feeling): something doesn't fit. 違和感がある / 違和感を覚える. Also physical: 目に違和感がある 'my eye feels funny'. A key mood word for the whole swap story.
cards.example_sentence: 新しい眼鏡をかけたら、しばらく違和感があった。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい めがね を かけたら、 しばらく いわかん が あった。
cards.example_meaning: When I put on my new glasses, they felt strange for a while.

cards.scene: 瀧 has no idea where he is or what to do, and the morning carries on around him anyway.
cards.context: Lit. 'to be lost at the door' (戸 + 惑う). Used when you don't know how to react to something new: 急な変化に戸惑う. Noun 戸惑い. Softer, more about uncertainty than 混乱 (total confusion).
cards.example_sentence: 初めての町で、バスの乗り方に戸惑った。
cards.example_reading: はじめて の まち で、 バス の のりかた に とまどった。
cards.example_meaning: In an unfamiliar town, I wasn't sure how to ride the bus.

cards.scene: Body, room and family all wrong — 瀧's head is in chaos, and 三葉 will wake up just as lost in Tokyo.
cards.context: 混乱する 'to be confused / thrown into chaos'; 頭が混乱する 'my head is spinning'. Works for people and for situations (交通が混乱する 'traffic is in chaos'). Stronger than 戸惑う.
cards.example_sentence: 急にいろいろなことを言われて、頭が混乱した。
cards.example_reading: きゅう に いろいろ な こと を いわれて、 あたま が こんらん した。
cards.example_meaning: I was told so many things at once that my head was spinning.

cards.scene: 瀧 stares hard at an unfamiliar girl's face in the mirror.
cards.context: Almost always まじまじと見る / 見つめる — staring because you can't believe what you see. Different from じろじろ (rude staring at others) and じっと (holding still and watching). Unrelated to the slang マジ.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は写真の中の自分をまじまじと見つめた。
cards.example_reading: かれ は しゃしん の なか の じぶん を まじまじと みつめた。
cards.example_meaning: He stared hard at himself in the photo.

cards.scene: The arms and fingers 瀧 looks down at are thin and delicate — nothing like his own.
cards.context: Irregular reading: 華 is normally か/はな and 奢 is normally しゃ/おごる. Used for slim, fragile-looking bodies or objects: 華奢な肩, 華奢なネックレス. Often written きゃしゃ.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は華奢に見えるが、実はとても力が強い。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は きゃしゃ に みえる が、 じつ は とても ちから が つよい。
cards.example_meaning: She looks delicate, but she's actually very strong.

cards.scene: 瀧 notices an unfamiliar weight on his chest and can't resist checking it.
cards.context: Noun from 膨らむ 'to swell' (パンが膨らむ, 夢が膨らむ 'a dream grows'). 胸の膨らみ is the polite, literary way prose refers to breasts. 膨 is a hard kanji — anchor the reading with ふくらむ.
cards.example_sentence: つぼみの膨らみに、春が近いことを感じた。
cards.example_reading: つぼみ の ふくらみ に、 はる が ちかい こと を かんじた。
cards.example_meaning: In the swelling of the buds, I felt that spring was near.

cards.scene: The famous comic beat — 瀧, sure it's a dream, checks 'his' new chest, which is not what a little sister wants to see at breakfast time.
cards.context: Basic sense: knead or squeeze with the hands — 肩を揉む 'massage someone's shoulders'. Idiom: 気を揉む 'to fret' (lit. knead one's spirit). 揉 is outside the common-use kanji list, so it is often written もむ.
cards.example_sentence: 疲れている母の肩を揉んであげた。
cards.example_reading: つかれて いる はは の かた を もんで あげた。
cards.example_meaning: I massaged my tired mother's shoulders.

cards.scene: The 'dream' feels far too real — the air, the floor, the body all register vividly.
cards.context: 生 (raw, alive) doubled: so fresh it still feels alive. 生々しい記憶, 生々しい傷. Often has a slightly unpleasant 'too real' edge, unlike the neutral 鮮やか (bright, vivid).
cards.example_sentence: 事故の記憶は、今でも生々しく残っている。
cards.example_reading: じこ の きおく は、 いま でも なまなましく のこって いる。
cards.example_meaning: The memory of the accident is still raw and vivid.

cards.scene: For a dream, everything feels oddly detailed — a feeling both heroes keep returning to.
cards.context: 妙 = strange, peculiar (妙な夢 'a weird dream'), but also 'exquisite' in 絶妙 (perfect timing/balance). 妙に静かだ, 妙に落ち着く — something is off but you can't say why. Narration loves it.
cards.example_sentence: 今日の教室は妙に静かだった。
cards.example_reading: きょう の きょうしつ は みょうに しずか だった。
cards.example_meaning: The classroom was strangely quiet today.

cards.simpler_synonym: びっくりして何も言えない
cards.scene: 四葉 finds her 'sister' acting bizarrely in the morning and is thoroughly unimpressed.
cards.context: Disbelief mixed with disgust or exasperation: 呆れた顔, 呆れて物も言えない 'so appalled I'm speechless'. Not plain surprise — there's always a judgment in it. Often written あきれる.
cards.example_sentence: 弟がまた宿題を忘れたと聞いて、母は呆れていた。
cards.example_reading: おとうと が また しゅくだい を わすれた と きいて、 はは は あきれて いた。
cards.example_meaning: Mother was exasperated to hear my little brother had forgotten his homework again.

cards.scene: At breakfast おばあちゃん looks at her granddaughter as if something isn't quite right.
cards.context: Almost always 怪訝な顔をする / 怪訝そうに — a puzzled, doubtful look at someone acting out of character. Irregular reading: 怪 is usually かい, and 訝 (as in 訝しい いぶかしい) is rare. Written register.
cards.example_sentence: 急に敬語で話し始めた兄を、妹は怪訝そうに見ていた。
cards.example_reading: きゅう に けいご で はなし はじめた あに を、 いもうと は けげん そう に みて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The younger sister looked dubiously at her brother, who had suddenly started speaking politely.

cards.scene: おばあちゃん seems to sense more than she says, as if she can see straight through 'Mitsuha'.
cards.context: 見 (see) + 透かす (let light through): to look right through a pretence. Usually passive: 心を見透かされる 'to have one's thoughts read'. Related 透明 (とうめい, transparent).
cards.example_sentence: 嘘をついても、母にはすぐ見透かされてしまう。
cards.example_reading: うそ を ついて も、 はは に は すぐ みすかされて しまう。
cards.example_meaning: Even if I lie, my mother sees right through me.

cards.scene: 瀧 has to get ready for school in someone else's body — uniform, hair, everything unfamiliar.
cards.context: 身 (body) + 支度 (preparation). Covers washing, dressing and doing your hair: 身支度を整える. 支度 alone = preparations in general (食事の支度 'getting a meal ready').
cards.example_sentence: 朝は五分で身支度を済ませて家を出る。
cards.example_reading: あさ は ごふん で みじたく を すませて いえ を でる。
cards.example_meaning: In the mornings I get ready in five minutes and leave the house.

cards.scene: 瀧 has no idea how to tie up 三葉's long hair, so he goes to school with it down.
cards.context: Mostly used for hair: 髪を結う. Same kanji as 結ぶ but read ゆう; past tense 結った (ゆった). 三葉 normally ties her hair with a braided cord, so loose hair is an instant sign something is off.
cards.example_sentence: 祭りの日、祖母が私の髪をきれいに結ってくれた。
cards.example_reading: まつり の ひ、 そぼ が わたし の かみ を きれい に ゆって くれた。
cards.example_meaning: On the festival day, my grandmother tied up my hair beautifully.

cards.scene: With nobody who knows how to tidy it, 三葉's hair stays a mess all day.
cards.context: ぼさぼさの髪 / 髪がぼさぼさだ — uncombed, untidy. Compare さらさら (silky, smooth) and ぼうぼう (overgrown — grass, beards).
cards.example_sentence: 寝坊したので、髪がぼさぼさのまま学校へ行った。
cards.example_reading: ねぼう した ので、 かみ が ぼさぼさ の まま がっこう へ いった。
cards.example_meaning: I overslept, so I went to school with my hair a mess.

cards.scene: The giveaway at school — each hero keeps using the wrong word for 'I'.
cards.context: 一 (one) + 人称 (grammatical person). 二人称 = second person (あなた, お前); 三人称 = third person. Japanese has many first-person words (わたし, 僕, 俺, あたし, うち), each signalling gender and attitude — see the grammar deck.
cards.example_sentence: 日本語には一人称がたくさんあって、話し手の性格が出る。
cards.example_reading: にほんご に は いちにんしょう が たくさん あって、 はなして の せいかく が でる。
cards.example_meaning: Japanese has many first-person pronouns, and they reveal the speaker's personality.

cards.scene: Classmates are thrown by 'Mitsuha's' rough, boyish way of talking — and 'Taki's' friends by his oddly soft one.
cards.context: 遣い comes from 遣う 'to use (with care)', with rendaku: つかい → づかい. 言葉遣いが悪い 'uses rude language'; 言葉遣いに気をつける 'mind one's language'. Same pattern: 金遣い (spending habits).
cards.example_sentence: 先生と話すときは、言葉遣いに気をつけなさい。
cards.example_reading: せんせい と はなす とき は、 ことばづかい に き を つけなさい。
cards.example_meaning: Watch your language when you talk to teachers.

cards.scene: 瀧 in 三葉's body sits, walks and talks with none of her usual care, and classmates find 'her' oddly crude.
cards.context: A な-adjective for someone loud, careless and unrefined: がさつな人, がさつな動作. Its traditional opposite is しとやか (graceful, ladylike) — the gap between the two is the joke of the swap.
cards.example_sentence: 兄はがさつに見えるが、実は細かいことによく気がつく。
cards.example_reading: あに は がさつ に みえる が、 じつ は こまかい こと に よく き が つく。
cards.example_meaning: My older brother seems crude, but he actually notices the little things.

cards.scene: Even small mannerisms give the swap away — 'Mitsuha' moves like a boy, 'Taki' like a girl.
cards.context: Small habitual movements that show who you are: かわいい仕草, 癖のある仕草. Also written 仕種. Different from ジェスチャー (deliberate signals).
cards.example_sentence: 髪を耳にかける仕草が、母にそっくりだ。
cards.example_reading: かみ を みみ に かける しぐさ が、 はは に そっくり だ。
cards.example_meaning: The way she tucks her hair behind her ear is exactly like her mother.

cards.scene: Classmates can't stop staring at 'Mitsuha', unable to make sense of how she's acting.
cards.context: じろじろ見る — staring openly in a way that makes the other person uncomfortable. Compare まじまじ (staring in disbelief) and ちらちら (glancing repeatedly).
cards.example_sentence: 変な服を着ていたので、電車の中でじろじろ見られた。
cards.example_reading: へん な ふく を きて いた ので、 でんしゃ の なか で じろじろ みられた。
cards.example_meaning: I was wearing weird clothes, so people stared at me on the train.

cards.scene: 三葉 wakes up in a boy's room in a Tokyo apartment where he lives with just his father.
cards.context: 父子 is read ふし here (not ちちこ). The counterpart is 母子家庭 (ぼしかてい, single-mother household); the neutral modern term is ひとり親家庭. 三葉's own home is also missing parents — a quiet parallel.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は父子家庭で育ったので、料理が得意だ。
cards.example_reading: かれ は ふしかてい で そだった ので、 りょうり が とくい だ。
cards.example_meaning: He grew up in a single-father household, so he's good at cooking.

cards.scene: Out the window and on the way to school, 三葉 sees the Tokyo skyline she has only ever seen on screens.
cards.context: 高層 = many-storied (層 = layer, floor). 高層マンション = high-rise apartment block; 超高層ビル = super-tall tower. Literary prose may use 摩天楼 (まてんろう) instead.
cards.example_sentence: 駅を出ると、目の前に高層ビルが並んでいた。
cards.example_reading: えき を でる と、 め の まえ に こうそう ビル が ならんで いた。
cards.example_meaning: When I came out of the station, high-rise buildings stood in rows before my eyes.

cards.scene: 三葉's first Tokyo commute — a crush of bodies unlike anything in her town.
cards.context: 満員 = full to capacity (満 full + 員 members); 満員御礼 = 'sold out, thank you'. 満員電車 is the fixed phrase for rush-hour trains. Compare 満席 (all seats taken).
cards.example_sentence: 毎朝の満員電車で、もう疲れてしまう。
cards.example_reading: まいあさ の まんいん でんしゃ で、 もう つかれて しまう。
cards.example_meaning: The packed train every morning wears me out before the day even starts.

cards.scene: Squeezed between strangers on the morning train, 三葉 can barely move.
cards.context: ぎゅうぎゅう詰め = crammed full; ぎゅうぎゅうに押し込む = cram in. A single ぎゅっと is a tight squeeze or hug. Compare すし詰め (packed like sushi).
cards.example_sentence: エレベーターは人でぎゅうぎゅうだった。
cards.example_reading: エレベーター は ひと で ぎゅうぎゅう だった。
cards.example_meaning: The elevator was jam-packed with people.

cards.scene: Station platforms and streets overflow with people — a sight unthinkable in her small town.
cards.context: Also written 人込み. 混む (to be crowded) with rendaku → ごみ. 人混みに紛れる 'blend into the crowd'; 人混みが苦手 'bad with crowds'.
cards.example_sentence: 人混みの中で、友達を見失ってしまった。
cards.example_reading: ひとごみ の なか で、 ともだち を みうしなって しまった。
cards.example_meaning: I lost sight of my friend in the crowd.

meanings: hustle and bustle of a crowd
cards.scene: The kind of word narration uses to paint the noise and motion of Tokyo streets around 三葉.
cards.context: 雑 (mixed) + 踏 (step): countless feet treading. A literary word for a crowded, noisy place: 都会の雑踏, 雑踏に紛れる. More atmospheric than 人混み.
cards.example_sentence: 都会の雑踏の中にいると、なぜか孤独を感じる。
cards.example_reading: とかい の ざっとう の なか に いる と、 なぜか こどく を かんじる。
cards.example_meaning: In the bustle of the city, I somehow feel lonely.

cards.scene: Cars, trains and people stream past in every direction around 三葉.
cards.context: Also read ゆきかう (more literary). 人々が行き交う, 車が行き交う — continuous traffic both ways. Different from すれ違う, which is two people passing each other once.
cards.example_sentence: 駅前の交差点を、たくさんの人が行き交っている。
cards.example_reading: えきまえ の こうさてん を、 たくさん の ひと が いきかって いる。
cards.example_meaning: Crowds of people are coming and going across the intersection in front of the station.

cards.scene: 三葉 gawks at everything — trains, signs, shop windows — like the newcomer she is.
cards.context: きょろきょろする — moving your eyes and head around because you're lost, curious or nervous. Compare うろうろ (wandering about on foot) and まじまじ (fixed, disbelieving stare).
cards.example_sentence: 初めて東京に来た弟は、駅でずっときょろきょろしていた。
cards.example_reading: はじめて とうきょう に きた おとうと は、 えき で ずっと きょろきょろ して いた。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother, in Tokyo for the first time, kept looking all around at the station.

meanings: to get carried away with excitement
cards.scene: Living out her dream of Tokyo, 三葉 can't contain her excitement.
cards.context: Behaving noisily and childishly because you're excited: 子供のようにはしゃぐ. Written in kana (the kanji 燥ぐ is rare). Can sound a little critical — 'getting carried away'.
cards.example_sentence: 雪を見た子供たちは、外ではしゃいでいた。
cards.example_reading: ゆき を みた こども たち は、 そと で はしゃいで いた。
cards.example_meaning: The children who saw the snow were romping around outside.

cards.simpler_synonym: すごすぎて何も言えない
cards.scene: The scale and speed of Tokyo leave 三葉 overwhelmed as well as thrilled.
cards.context: 圧 (pressure) + 倒 (topple). Active 圧倒する 'to overwhelm, crush (an opponent)'; 圧倒的 'overwhelming' (圧倒的な人気). The passive is the usual way to say a sight or a person blew you away.
cards.example_sentence: 初めて海を見たとき、その大きさに圧倒された。
cards.example_reading: はじめて うみ を みた とき、 その おおきさ に あっとう された。
cards.example_meaning: When I first saw the sea, I was overwhelmed by its size.

cards.scene: The cafés and shops 三葉 visits after school feel impossibly stylish and grown-up.
cards.context: Usually 洗練された 'refined, polished': 洗練されたデザイン, 洗練された店. 洗 (wash) + 練 (knead, refine) — washed and worked until smooth.
cards.example_sentence: その店は小さいが、洗練された雰囲気がある。
cards.example_reading: その みせ は ちいさい が、 せんれん された ふんいき が ある。
cards.example_meaning: The shop is small, but it has a refined atmosphere.

cards.scene: 司 and 高木 stare open-mouthed as 'Taki' fumbles for the right word for 'I'.
cards.context: ぽかんとする / 口をぽかんと開ける — frozen with a blank face because you can't follow what's happening. Compare ぼうっと (spaced out, daydreaming).
cards.example_sentence: 突然の話に、みんなぽかんとしていた。
cards.example_reading: とつぜん の はなし に、 みんな ぽかんと して いた。
cards.example_meaning: Everyone just stared blankly at the sudden news.

cards.scene: Under her new friends' puzzled looks, 三葉's explanations come out in a flustered jumble.
cards.context: しどろもどろになる / しどろもどろに答える — speech falling apart because you're panicking or have been caught out. It even sounds tangled and stumbling.
cards.example_sentence: 先生に急に質問されて、しどろもどろになった。
cards.example_reading: せんせい に きゅう に しつもん されて、 しどろもどろ に なった。
cards.example_meaning: When the teacher suddenly asked me a question, I got flustered and tongue-tied.

cards.scene: わたし… no, 僕… no, 俺 — 三葉 keeps correcting herself mid-sentence.
cards.context: Vます-stem + 直す = redo: 書き直す (rewrite), やり直す (start over). 言い直す is fixing what you just said: 〜と言い直した.
cards.example_sentence: 名前を間違えたので、あわてて言い直した。
cards.example_reading: なまえ を まちがえた ので、 あわてて いいなおした。
cards.example_meaning: I got the name wrong, so I hurriedly corrected myself.

cards.scene: Everything 'Taki' does with his friends — talking, walking, joking — comes out stiff and unnatural.
cards.context: For movements, smiles, conversations or relationships that aren't smooth: ぎこちない笑顔, 二人の間がぎこちない. It's one adjective — not a negative of some word ぎこち.
cards.example_sentence: 久しぶりに会ったので、最初は会話がぎこちなかった。
cards.example_reading: ひさしぶり に あった ので、 さいしょ は かいわ が ぎこちなかった。
cards.example_meaning: We hadn't met in ages, so the conversation was awkward at first.

cards.scene: The everyday slang of 瀧 and his friends at school and at work.
cards.context: Short for 真面目 (まじめ). マジで？ 'Seriously?', マジかよ 'No way!' (rough), マジでうまい 'really tasty'. Usually katakana; very casual — never with teachers or bosses.
cards.example_sentence: え、マジで？明日テストなの？
cards.example_reading: え、 マジ で？ あした テスト な の？
cards.example_meaning: Wait, seriously? There's a test tomorrow?

cards.simpler_synonym: お金をたくさん使うこと
cards.scene: Fancy pancakes at a stylish café cost more than 三葉 can believe — an extravagance by her town's standards.
cards.context: な-adjective and noun: 贅沢な食事, 贅沢を言う 'to be picky, ask for too much'. Both kanji are hard; note 貝 (shell = money) at the bottom of 贅.
cards.example_sentence: たまには贅沢をして、高いレストランに行こう。
cards.example_reading: たま に は ぜいたく を して、 たかい レストラン に いこう。
cards.example_meaning: Let's treat ourselves once in a while and go to an expensive restaurant.

cards.scene: 三葉 gazes dreamily at the cafés, sweets and stylish people of Tokyo.
cards.context: うっとりする / うっとりと見とれる — lost in admiration of something beautiful. Compare ぼうっと (spaced out, with no admiration involved).
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は美しい夜景にうっとりしていた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は うつくしい やけい に うっとり して いた。
cards.example_meaning: She was entranced by the beautiful night view.

cards.scene: 三葉 has to cover 瀧's waiter shift at an Italian restaurant with no idea what she's doing.
cards.context: 接 (contact) + 客 (customer). 接客業 = the service industry; 接客態度 = attitude toward customers. A standard word in part-time-job talk.
cards.example_sentence: 接客のアルバイトで、敬語が上手になった。
cards.example_reading: せっきゃく の アルバイト で、 けいご が じょうず に なった。
cards.example_meaning: My customer-service job made me better at polite Japanese.

cards.scene: A rude customer at the restaurant starts making trouble.
cards.context: False friend: Japanese クレーム means a complaint, not a 'claim'. クレームをつける 'to make a complaint'; a habitual complainer is a クレーマー. Neutral synonym: 苦情 (くじょう).
cards.example_sentence: 店員の態度にクレームをつける客がいた。
cards.example_reading: てんいん の たいど に クレーム を つける きゃく が いた。
cards.example_meaning: There was a customer complaining about a staff member's attitude.

cards.scene: A customer starts hassling the staff, and the evening shift turns ugly.
cards.context: Basic sense 'to get tangled' (糸が絡む). 人に絡む = to pick on someone, often drunkenly or aggressively: 酔っ払いに絡まれた. Also 'to be involved in' (事件に絡む).
cards.example_sentence: 帰り道で、知らない男に絡まれて怖かった。
cards.example_reading: かえりみち で、 しらない おとこ に からまれて こわかった。
cards.example_meaning: On the way home, a strange man hassled me, and I was scared.

cards.scene: The customer slashes 奥寺先輩's skirt with a knife — the shocking moment of 三葉's shift.
cards.context: 切る (cut) + 裂く (tear). Violent and sudden: 布を切り裂く; also figurative, 静けさを切り裂く悲鳴 'a scream that tears the silence'. Related 裂ける 'to split, tear (by itself)'.
cards.example_sentence: 雷の光が、夜空を切り裂いた。
cards.example_reading: かみなり の ひかり が、 よぞら を きりさいた。
cards.example_meaning: A flash of lightning ripped across the night sky.

cards.scene: 奥寺先輩 is left with a tear in her skirt in the middle of her shift.
cards.context: 裂ける (to tear) + 目 (point, spot) — like 割れ目 (crack) and 切れ目 (cut, break). For clothes, 破れ目 / 破れたところ is more everyday.
cards.example_sentence: ズボンの裂け目から、ひざが見えていた。
cards.example_reading: ズボン の さけめ から、 ひざ が みえて いた。
cards.example_meaning: My knee was showing through the tear in my trousers.

cards.scene: Sewing is something 三葉 is good at — and in 瀧's body it saves the day at the restaurant.
cards.context: 裁 (cut cloth) + 縫 (sew). 裁縫が得意 'good at sewing'; 裁縫箱 = sewing box. 裁 also appears in 裁判 (trial) — 'cutting' a judgment.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母に教わったおかげで、裁縫が得意になった。
cards.example_reading: そぼ に おそわった おかげ で、 さいほう が とくい に なった。
cards.example_meaning: Thanks to my grandmother teaching me, I became good at sewing.

cards.scene: 三葉, in 瀧's body, sews up the damaged skirt on the spot.
cards.context: 縫い目 (seam), 縫い物 (sewing work), 傷口を縫う (stitch a wound). Figurative: 人混みを縫って歩く 'weave through a crowd'. Pairs with 結う and 編む in the story's thread-and-cord vocabulary.
cards.example_sentence: とれたボタンを自分で縫いつけた。
cards.example_reading: とれた ボタン を じぶん で ぬいつけた。
cards.example_meaning: I sewed the button that had come off back on myself.

cards.scene: Instead of a plain repair, the tear is turned into a pretty embroidered design.
cards.context: 刺 (pierce) + 繍 (embroider). 刺繍する / 刺繍を入れる 'to embroider (a design on)'. 繍 is a rare kanji you'll basically only meet in this word — learn ししゅう as a unit.
cards.example_sentence: ハンカチに花の刺繍を入れてプレゼントした。
cards.example_reading: ハンカチ に はな の ししゅう を いれて プレゼント した。
cards.example_meaning: I embroidered flowers on a handkerchief and gave it as a present.

cards.scene: Everyone watches as 'Taki' fixes the skirt with surprising speed and skill.
cards.context: 手際がいい / 手際よく — doing a job quickly and neatly. 不手際 = mishandling, a blunder (common in apologies: 不手際がありました).
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は手際よく夕食の準備を済ませた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は てぎわ よく ゆうしょく の じゅんび を すませた。
cards.example_meaning: She deftly finished getting dinner ready.

cards.scene: Nobody expected 瀧 to be so good with a needle and thread.
cards.context: 手先が器用 'good with one's hands'. Opposite 不器用 — also used for people who are socially clumsy (不器用な性格). 器用貧乏 = jack of all trades, master of none.
cards.example_sentence: 兄は手先が器用で、何でも自分で直してしまう。
cards.example_reading: あに は てさき が きよう で、 なんでも じぶん で なおして しまう。
cards.example_meaning: My brother is good with his hands and fixes everything himself.

meanings: to see in a new light
cards.scene: After the sewing rescue, 奥寺先輩 sees the boy she works with in a new, warmer light.
cards.context: Two senses: 'check again' (答えを見直す) and 'revise one's opinion upward' (彼を見直した 'I think better of him now'). The second is what happens when someone surprises you in a good way.
cards.example_sentence: 困っている人を助ける姿を見て、彼を見直した。
cards.example_reading: こまって いる ひと を たすける すがた を みて、 かれ を みなおした。
cards.example_meaning: Seeing him help someone in trouble, I thought much better of him.

cards.scene: The distant, popular senior begins to relax and chat with 'Taki'.
cards.context: Lit. 'to melt / loosen'. 〜と打ち解ける; 打ち解けた雰囲気 'a relaxed atmosphere'. It's about walls coming down between people, not just getting acquainted.
cards.example_sentence: 転校生はすぐにクラスのみんなと打ち解けた。
cards.example_reading: てんこうせい は すぐ に クラス の みんな と うちとけた。
cards.example_meaning: The transfer student quickly warmed up to everyone in the class.

cards.scene: A word that fits the irony of 'Taki' out-sewing everyone — he suddenly seems full of feminine skills.
cards.context: Modern slang (2000s on) for skills stereotypically called feminine: cooking, sewing, grooming, style. 女子力が高い is used playfully, even about boys. Casual, and a little old-fashioned in its assumptions.
cards.example_sentence: 毎日お弁当を作るなんて、女子力が高いね。
cards.example_reading: まいにち お べんとう を つくる なんて、 じょしりょく が たかい ね。
cards.example_meaning: You make a packed lunch every day? You're so domestic!

cards.scene: Back in their own bodies, each remembers the 'dream' only in vague, fading pieces.
cards.context: 曖昧な記憶 (hazy memory), 曖昧な返事 (noncommittal answer). Both kanji have the sun radical 日 — think 'dim light'. Very common in speech and writing.
cards.example_sentence: 子供のころの記憶は、もう曖昧になっている。
cards.example_reading: こども の ころ の きおく は、 もう あいまい に なって いる。
cards.example_meaning: My childhood memories have already become hazy.

cards.scene: Like any dream, the details slip away soon after waking.
cards.context: 記憶が薄れる, 関心が薄れる (interest wanes), 霧が薄れる (mist thins). A gradual fading; 薄まる is more for liquids being diluted.
cards.example_sentence: 時間がたつにつれて、悲しみは少しずつ薄れていった。
cards.example_reading: じかん が たつ に つれて、 かなしみ は すこし ずつ うすれて いった。
cards.example_meaning: As time passed, the sadness gradually faded.

cards.scene: Each finds diary entries on their phone that they never wrote — notes left by the other.
cards.context: You know the word; in this story the 日記 is a phone diary app that becomes two strangers' message board. 日記をつける 'keep a diary'; 日記帳 = diary book; 絵日記 = picture diary.
cards.example_sentence: 寝る前に、その日のことを日記に書いている。
cards.example_reading: ねる まえ に、 その ひ の こと を にっき に かいて いる。
cards.example_meaning: Before bed, I write about the day in my diary.

cards.scene: Strange entries turn up in their phones and notebooks, written in someone else's style.
cards.context: From 書き込む 'to write in, fill in'. Used for notes in a book's margins, entries on a form, and posts on forums or social media (ネットの書き込み).
cards.example_sentence: 教科書に、知らない人の書き込みがあった。
cards.example_reading: きょうかしょ に、 しらない ひと の かきこみ が あった。
cards.example_meaning: There were notes by someone I didn't know written in my textbook.

cards.scene: The handwriting in the notebook is clearly not their own — proof that someone else was there.
cards.context: 筆 (brush) + 跡 (trace, mark). Used when identifying who wrote something: 筆跡が似ている, 筆跡鑑定 (handwriting analysis). Everyday word: 字 (彼の字はきれい).
cards.example_sentence: この手紙の筆跡は、間違いなく父のものだ。
cards.example_reading: この てがみ の ひっせき は、 まちがいなく ちち の もの だ。
cards.example_meaning: The handwriting in this letter is definitely my father's.

cards.scene: Words scrawled on skin or in a notebook greet them after waking, as if someone else had been using their body.
cards.context: 落 (drop) + 書き: writing 'dropped' where it doesn't belong. 壁に落書きする (graffiti), ノートの落書き (doodles). Pen marks on your own hand that you didn't make are its creepiest form.
cards.example_sentence: 弟が私のノートに落書きをした。
cards.example_reading: おとうと が わたし の ノート に らくがき を した。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother scribbled in my notebook.

cards.scene: Friends say you acted strangely yesterday — and you have no idea what they mean.
cards.context: Almost always 心当たりがある / ない: 'I have (no) idea who or what it could be.' A classic question from police or worried friends: 何か心当たりはない？ Verb version: 思い当たる.
cards.example_sentence: 財布をどこに置いたか、まったく心当たりがない。
cards.example_reading: さいふ を どこ に おいた か、 まったく こころあたり が ない。
cards.example_meaning: I have absolutely no idea where I put my wallet.

cards.scene: Finding messages you didn't write and hearing about a day you can't remember is more than a little creepy.
cards.context: 不 (not) + 気味 (feeling); 不 is read ぶ here, as in 不用心 and 不細工. Compare 気味が悪い (same meaning, more conversational) and 気味 in 風邪気味 'a bit of a cold'.
cards.example_sentence: 誰もいないはずの部屋から音がして、不気味だった。
cards.example_reading: だれ も いない はず の へや から おと が して、 ぶきみ だった。
cards.example_meaning: A sound came from a room that should have been empty — it was eerie.

meanings: to be embarrassed (in front of others)
to make a fool of oneself
cards.simpler_synonym: 恥ずかしい思いをする
cards.scene: Each learns, too late, how badly 'they' embarrassed themselves while the other was in charge.
cards.context: 恥 (shame) + かく (to 'break out in', as in 汗をかく). 人前で恥をかく 'embarrass oneself in public'; 恥をかかせる 'to humiliate someone'. The shame happens to you — not something you do on purpose.
cards.example_sentence: 名前を読み間違えて、みんなの前で恥をかいた。
cards.example_reading: なまえ を よみまちがえて、 みんな の まえ で はじ を かいた。
cards.example_meaning: I misread the name and embarrassed myself in front of everyone.

cards.simpler_synonym: びっくりして落ち着かない
cards.scene: Hearing about things they don't remember doing leaves both of them shaken.
cards.context: 動 (move) + 揺 (shake): the heart wobbling. 動揺する / 動揺を隠す 'hide one's agitation'. Don't confuse with 童謡 (どうよう, children's song) — same reading.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は突然の知らせに動揺して、言葉が出なかった。
cards.example_reading: かれ は とつぜん の しらせ に どうよう して、 ことば が でなかった。
cards.example_meaning: Shaken by the sudden news, he couldn't find any words.

cards.simpler_synonym: 信じていいかわからない
cards.scene: Is it really just a dream? Both heroes start to wonder, only half believing the answer.
cards.context: Four-character idiom (四字熟語): 半 (half) 信 (believe) 半 疑 (doubt). 半信半疑で聞く 'listen half-believing'. Same build as 半死半生 (half dead).
cards.example_sentence: 友達の話を半信半疑で聞いていたが、本当だった。
cards.example_reading: ともだち の はなし を はんしんはんぎ で きいて いた が、 ほんとう だった。
cards.example_meaning: I listened to my friend's story half in doubt, but it turned out to be true.

cards.scene: The notes, the phone entries and the friends' reports pile up as proof the 'dream' was real.
cards.context: 証拠がある / 証拠を残す 'leave evidence'. 〜のが何よりの証拠だ 'the best proof is that…'. Related 証明 (proof in logic or maths), 保証 (guarantee).
cards.example_sentence: 彼が嘘をついているという証拠は、どこにもない。
cards.example_reading: かれ が うそ を ついて いる と いう しょうこ は、 どこ に も ない。
cards.example_meaning: There is no evidence anywhere that he is lying.

cards.simpler_synonym: きっとそうだと思うこと
cards.scene: Doubt slowly turns into certainty: this is no ordinary dream.
cards.context: 確信する / 確信を持つ / 確信に変わる 'turn into certainty'. Different from 自信 (self-confidence). Colloquially, 確信犯 = someone who does wrong knowingly.
cards.example_sentence: 彼の目を見て、彼が犯人だと確信した。
cards.example_reading: かれ の め を みて、 かれ が はんにん だ と かくしん した。
cards.example_meaning: Looking into his eyes, I was convinced he was the culprit.

meanings: to trade places with each other
cards.scene: The chapter's big realisation — when they sleep, the boy and the girl swap bodies.
cards.context: 入れる + 替わる: one goes in as the other comes out. Noun 入れ替わり is the story's word for the body swap. Transitive 入れ替える 'to replace, swap (something)': 空気を入れ替える 'to air out a room'.
cards.example_sentence: 席替えで、私と彼女の席が入れ替わった。
cards.example_reading: せきがえ で、 わたし と かのじょ の せき が いれかわった。
cards.example_meaning: In the seat change, she and I swapped places.
